name: fastfetch-aaa9153f-blind16
instr:
# fastfetch: repairing sixteen injected faults without a test suite

The repository has received 16 separate undocumented edits.

A program run from a shell prompt that gathers facts about the machine it runs on and prints them as a tidy report now gets a great many of those facts wrong. Nothing about the machine changed and nothing about how the program is invoked changed. The same invocations that used to produce correct output now produce wrong output, and in a few places what used to be an answer comes back empty.

Start with what the program is handed to work from. Text written in the printable encoding built from letters, digits, plus and slash turns back into the wrong bytes whenever certain digit characters appear, so a payload written out in that form no longer reads back as what went in. Pulling a named setting and its value out of a row of configuration-style text hands back the wrong piece of the row: rather than stepping over the blanks that separate the two, it eats the value's own characters, so what comes back starts with a blank or is empty. A shade asked for by name on the command line turns into an escape sequence carrying a wrong byte, so whatever is printed in it shows up in an unintended shade. Asking which visual styling the user picked, as recorded in the preference files the desktop widget library keeps, comes back empty whenever only the newest release of that library has one recorded.
